paper.title_en: $α$--$α$ Correlations in Excited Clustering Nuclei Across the Solid-Liquid Transition
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the structural evolution of $α$-cluster matter using a microscopic transport model for four $α$-conjugate collision systems, including $^{12}\text{C}+^{12}\text{C}$, $^{16}\text{O}+^{12}\text{C}$, $^{28}\text{Si}+^{12}\text{C}$, and $^{40}\text{Ca}+^{12}\text{C}$ at incident energies ranging from 2.0 to 7.0~MeV/u. The $α$-cluster structure of an excited nucleus undergoes a solid-liquid phase transition with increasing incident energy. Whether it proceeds by the dissociation of individual clusters or by the collapse of their spatial organization remains unexplored, as does the question of whether any characteristic $α$--$α$ correlation survives. The one-body density $ρ(\mathbf{r})$, the standard clustering diagnostic, cannot by itself settle this question, since it neither distinguishes a genuine cluster configuration from a density fluctuation nor reveals the sparse residual clusters masked by the surrounding nucleon medium. We therefore construct the exclusive $α$--$α$ two-body spatial correlation function from the $α$-cluster centroids to isolate the $α$ clusters. In all four systems the $α$--$α$ correlation exhibits two peaks, a nearest-neighbor one and a next-nearest-neighbor inter-cluster one. Both peak positions increase with system size. Over the energy range studied, which spans this transition, the mean number of $α$ clusters per event falls steeply while the $α$--$α$ correlation persists and the inter-cluster distances change only slightly. The individual clusters therefore dissociate rather than lose their spatial organization.
